title: Declared crop regions: which rect on a spec-pile sheet a citation is about
notes: A spec-pile citation names a document and a sheet and nothing finer -- the pile is append-only, the filename is the identity, and there is no zone to pin (scripts/build_viewer_crops.py's spec_pile rule). So a fastener card showed a whole photocopied sheet carrying a sixty-four-row table when the citation was about one row of it. Jeff, 2026-09-14: 'Currently datasheet cross refs (for fasteners) just display the entire spec sheet which often has large tables with dozens of rows.' Option B of that session: a registry of declared regions, because a region is reused across stacks and because source_ref stays untouched.

Declared configuration, never fuzzy matching -- the docs/topologies/part_mesh_aliases.json precedent. Nothing here is found by searching a page: somebody rendered the sheet, looked at it, and recorded the rect with scripts/record_spec_crop_region.py. Each entry's `shows` is its evidence, in the same sense a stack element's source_ref is: a region that claims to be the cited row and is not is a wrong number wearing the right format.
`rect` is [x0, y0, x1, y1] in PDF points, origin top-left -- the PyMuPDF convention, and the same one crops.json reports as rect_pt.

`match` is the citation text a region answers to, tested against the where-ref fields named by tolerance_stack.spec_crop_regions.WHERE_REF_FIELDS plus the element's hardware_ref. Longest declared match wins; a tie between two regions is ambiguous and crops nothing; a page carrying exactly one region uses it. A citation that matches nothing keeps the whole-sheet crop it would have had anyway -- nothing is invented.

Consumed by scripts/build_viewer_crops.py for any citation whose resolved PDF lives in data/inbox/specs/, whichever rule named the document (spec_pile by filename, or a source_ref.export that points into the pile). The crop entry records the region it used as located_by: "declared_region". Shape and live matching are pinned by tests/test_spec_crop_regions.py.

regions.label: NAS6403 row of the sheet-1 dimension table
regions.shows: Sheet 1's dimension table: its column headers (BASIC NUMBER, Nom Thread Size, C, D Dia unplated/plated-before/plated-after, E Dia Min, H, J, K Dia, M) and the NAS6403 row beneath them -- .1900-32, C .376/.367, E .335, H .125/.110, J .088/.073, K .056/.046, M .174/.154. Columns right of M (N, P, R Rad, T, TD) are outside the rect; the whole sheet stays one click away on the card. Read off a 7x render of sheet 1 on 2026-09-14.
